title: lock, Interlocked, and primitives
hook: lock is mutual exclusion plus a memory barrier. Interlocked is a single atomic instruction. volatile is neither. On .NET 10 you should lock a dedicated System.Threading.Lock.

sections.heading: What lock compiles to
sections.prose: For a System.Threading.Lock target (C# 13 / .NET 9+), lock calls EnterScope and disposes the scope in finally. For any other reference, it is Monitor.Enter/Exit in a finally. Recursion on the same thread is allowed. Microsoft’s best practices: dedicated private instance, never typeof(T), never this, never a string interned by other code. Keep the body tiny and CPU-only. Mutex is a kernel, cross-process name; it is for a single-instance desktop tool, not for request-level Redis. SemaphoreSlim is a counting gate that has WaitAsync, so you can throttle 8 concurrent origin fills without blocking a pool thread while waiting to enter — still release in finally, still do not treat it as a substitute for unbounded I/O inside the gate without timeouts.

snippets.label: C# 13 Lock for memory state; Interlocked for a counter
snippets.explanation: The dictionary needs mutual exclusion. The counter only needs Interlocked. Neither path calls Redis inside the lock.

sections.heading: volatile’s narrow, discouraged role
sections.prose: volatile tells the C# compiler and runtime not to cache a field in a register across reads in some cases. Microsoft’s current language reference warns that it is misunderstood: no atomic ++, no mutual exclusion, no guaranteed immediate visibility on every processor for every pattern. You cannot mark long or double volatile. Prefer Interlocked.Read/Exchange or a lock. The old Worker _shouldStop sample still appears in docs; in new code a CancellationToken or Interlocked.Exchange on an int flag is clearer. ReaderWriterLockSlim is for rare read-heavy in-memory maps; ConcurrentDictionary is usually simpler.

interviewTakeaways: lock = exclusive section + barrier. Interlocked = atomic RMW. volatile = weak ordering hint.
Lock a private System.Threading.Lock (or object on older TFMs).
commonPitfalls: Using volatile int and ++ for a shared attempt counter.
introducedIn: System.Threading.Lock with lock statement in C# 13 / .NET 9

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS on one thread does not need lock for objects. Across workers, Atomics are the Interlocked analog. There is no language lock statement.
